stem: The motto of Defence Research and Development Organisation is :
expl: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is the premier agency under the Department of Defence Research and Development in Ministry of Defence of the Government of India, charged with the military's research and development, headquartered in Delhi, India. DRDO was formed in 1958 from the amalgamation of the then already functioning Technical Development Establishment (TDEs) of the Indian Army and the Directorate of Technical Development and Production (DTDP) with the Defence Science Organization (DSO). The motto of DRDO is : "Balasya Mulam Vigyanam" – the source of strength is science – which drives the nation in peace and war.

stem: Where did the Indian Army establish a Quantum Laboratory in Madhya Pradesh in 2021?
expl: Indian armed forces are doing dedicated investment in quantum technologies for some time now. During 2021, Indian Army set up a Quantum Computing Laboratory at Military College of Telecommunication Engineering, Mhow, Madhya Pradesh. This laboratory has been established with the help of the National Security Council Secretariat (NSCS). Research undertaken by Indian Army in the field of Quantum Technology will help leapfrog into next generation communication and transform the current system of cryptography in the Indian Armed Forces to Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC).

stem: Mission 'Divyastra' is related to which of the following?

Various Telemetry and radar stations tracked and monitored multiple re-entry vehicles. The Mission accomplished the designed parameters. MIRV is an exoatmospheric ballistic missile payload containing several warheads, each capable of being aimed to hit a different target.

stem: What is the name of the manportable air defence system developed by 'DRDO' to neutralize aerial threats?
expl: The Very Short-Range Air Defence System, or VSHORADS, is a 4th Generation, technically-advanced miniaturized, man-portable air-defence system (MANPADS) developed by Research Centre Imarat (RCI), a research lab under Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), located in Hyderabad. Multiple DRDO laboratories along with Indian industry partners are participating in the project. It is designed for anti-aircraft warfare and neutralising low altitude aerial threats at short ranges. Recently, on February 1, 2025, DRDO has successfully conducted three successive flight-trials of VSHORADS from Chandipur off the coast of Odisha. Earlier, DRDO successfully conducted three flight-tests of VSHORADS at the Pokhran Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan on October 3 and 4, 2024.

stem: Which of the following statements are true about Akashteer?

options.label: a

options.label: b
options.text: It seamlessly integrates India's larger C4ISR

options.label: c
options.text: It reflects a strategic shift from passive defence to proactive retaliation

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Akashteer is the 'core' command-and-control mechanism of the Army’s air-defence system, through which various air-defence units, radars, and weapon systems are connected as a network. Akashteer works in an integrated manner with India’s larger C4ISR (Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance) ecosystem and enables all three services to operate in a coordinated way. It automatically monitors the low-altitude airspace and efficiently controls ground-based air-defence weapon systems, leading to a shift in India’s strategy from passive defence to active, swift counter-response. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

stem:
Consider the following aircraft:
1. Rafael 2. MiG-29
3. Tejas MK-1 How many of the above are considered fifth generation fighter aircraft?
expl: Fifth generation fighter aircrafts include major technologies developed during the first part of the 21st century. As of 2024, these are the most advanced fighters in operation. The characteristics of a fifth generation fighter aircraft are not universally agreed upon, and not every fifth generation type necessarily has them all; however, they typically include stealth, low-probability-of-intercept radar (LPIR), agile airframes with supercruise performance, advanced avionics features, and highly integrated computer systems capable of networking with other elements within the battlespace for situational awareness and C³ (command, control and communications) capabilities. Examples of combat-ready fifth generation fighter aircrafts include the Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor and Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II (USA), Chengdu J-20 (China), and Sukhoi Su-57(Russia). Rafael is referred to as an ‘omnirole’ 4.5th generation aircraft developed by France’s Dassault Aviation. The MiG-29 is a 4th generation fighter jet developed by Russia (Former Soviet Union). The Tejas MK-1 is an indigenously designed and developed multirole Indian fighter jet, but it too falls under the 4.5th generation. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

stem:
With reference to Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), consider the following statements :
I. All types of UAVs can do vertical landing.
II. All types of UAVs can do automated hovering.
III. All types of UAVs can use battery only as a source of power supply. How many of the statements given above are correct?
expl: UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) are mainly classified into four types based on their design and flight mechanics: Multi-rotor such as quadcopters, hexacopters, and octocopters (highly maneuverable), Fixed-wing (long-range/endurance), Single-rotor (heavy-lift), and Fixed-wing Hybrid VTOL (combining vertical lift with efficient forward flight). Only multi-rotor and VTOL or hybrid types of UAVs are capable of vertical take-off and landing. UAVs with fixed-wing require runways or catapult systems for takeoff and landing. Therefore, Statement I is incorrect. Hovering refers to maintaining a stationary position in the air without moving forward or backward. Automated hovering means the UAV can maintain its position without manual input. Again, only certain types of UAVs can do this. Multi-rotor or helicopter-type UAVs have the ability to hover in the air, while fixed-wing UAVs cannot hover because they depend on constant forward movement to generate lift. Hence, Statement II is also incorrect. Statement III is also incorrect as not all UAVs rely solely on batteries for power supply. Small UAVs run on batteries (usually lithium-polymer or lithium-ion), while Larger UAVs use Internal Combustion (petrol/diesel) or hybrid engines to provide higher energy density, allowing for longer flight times. Some UAVs also use fuel cell-power for high energy efficiency and are used in specialized applications. Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

stem: Which one of the following statements best reflects the idea behind the 'Fractional Orbital Bombardment System' often talked about in media?

options.text: A missile is put into a stable orbit around the Earth and deorbits over a target on the Earth.

expl: The idea behind Fractional Orbital Bombardment System (FOBS) is, a warhead delivery system (missile) is put into a stable orbit around the Earth and it deorbits over a target on the Earth. A FOBS is a warhead delivery system that uses a Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) towards its target destination. Just before reaching the target, it deorbits through a retrograde engine burn. This allows it to slow down so that its trajectory intersects with its target on the ground. The Soviet Union first developed FOBS as a nuclear weapons delivery system in the 1960s. It was one of the first Soviet efforts to use space to deliver nuclear weapons. In August 2021, China tested a weapon that combined a FOBS with a hypersonic glide vehicle (HGV).

stem: The 'New START Treaty' was in the news. What is in this treaty?

options.label: a

expl: The 'New START' (START : Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty) is the treaty between the United States of America and the Russian Federation on measures for the further reduction and limitation of strategic offensive arms. It was signed on 8 April, 2010 in Prague by Former Russian president Dmitry Medvedev and then American President Barack Obama. Under the terms of the treaty, the number of strategic missile launchers will be reduced by half and it limits the number of deployed strategic nuclear warheads to 1550. It came into force on 5 February, 2011. On 21 February, 2023, Russia suspended its participation in New START. However, it did not withdraw from the treaty, and clarified that it would continue to abide by the numerical limits in the treaty. The new START was officially expired on 5 February, 2026.

stem: Which one of the following is incorrect about India’s Disarmament Policy in recent decades ?

options.label: a
options.text: India is a party to all five protocols of the CCW.

options.label: b
options.text: India does not support negotiations in the CD on FMCT.

options.label: d
options.text: India is not a signatory to CTBT.

expl: India signed the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in 1981 and ratified it in 1984. As a High Contracting Party, India is committed to all five of its Protocols, which regulate or prohibit conventional weapons deemed excessively injurious, such as landmines and incendiary weapons, aiming to balance humanitarian concerns with military necessity. India supports the immediate commencement of negotiations on a universal, non-discriminatory, and internationally verifiable Fissile Material Cutoff Treaty (FMCT) within the Conference on Disarmament (CD), based on the 1995 Shannon report mandating that the treaty ban future production of fissile materials for weapons. India is a party to the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) and an active member of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW). India signed the treaty on January 14, 1993, and ratified it in 1996, with the CWC coming into force for India in 1997. India also enacted the CWC Act, 2000. India is not a signatory to the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) of 1996, primarily citing its discriminatory nature. India argues the treaty does not mandate universal disarmament, undermines national security, and restricts its strategic autonomy, opting instead for a credible minimum deterrent. Hence, statement of option (b) is incorrect, while other three options are correct.

1. The 'Australia Group' is an informal arrangement which aims to allow exporting countries to minimize the risk of assisting chemical and biological weapons proliferation, whereas the 'Wassenaar Arrangement' is a formal group under the OECD holding identical objectives.
2. The 'Australia Group' comprises predominantly of Asian, African and North American countries whereas the member countries of 'Wassenaar Arrangement' are predominantly from the European Union and American continents.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: The Australia Group in an informal group of countries established in 1985 (after the use of chemical weapons by Iraq in 1984) to help member countries to identify those exports which need to be controlled so as not to contribute to the spread of chemical and biological weapons. Now it has 43 members including all 27 members of the European Union, UK, the European Commission, USA and Canada etc. Japan, South Korea, Turkiye and India are Asian Countries in this group while it has no member from African continent. The Wassenaar Arrangement has been established in order to contribute to regional and international security and stability by promoting transparency and greater responsibility in the transfer of conventional arms and dual-use goods and technology. The Wassenaar Arrangement is presently composed of 42 countries. It consists mainly European Union countries (and UK, Russia, Ukraine etc.) and countries of American Continent (Japan, South Korea, Turkiye and India are Asian countries in it while South Africa is the only country from African continent). Now, through this explanation it is clear that the second part of statement 1 and the first part of the Statement 2 is incorrect. Thus, the correct answer is option (d).

expl: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), also called the North Atlantic Alliance, is an intergovernmental military alliance of 32 member States — 30 European and 2 North American. Established in the aftermath of World War II, the organization implements the North Atlantic Treaty, signed in Washington, D.C. on 4 April, 1949. NATO is a collective security system : its independent member States agree to defend each other against attacks by third parties. NATO formed with twelve founding members and has added new members ten times, most recently when Sweden joined the alliance on 7 March, 2024. In addition, NATO currently recognizes Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, and Ukraine as aspiring members. NATO's main headquarters are located in Brussels, Belgium, while NATO's military headquarters are near Mons, Belgium. Hence, only statement II is correct.

expl: The Eighth edition of the bilateral Japan-India Maritime Exercise 2024 (JIMEX-24) took place in Yokosuka, Japan in June, 2024. This naval exercise involved harbour and sea phases, with professional, sports, and social activities at the harbour, followed by joint naval war drills at sea to improve their interoperability across various operations. The Indian Navy was represented by Stealth Frigate INS Shivalik and the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF) was represented by the Guided Missile Destroyer JS Yugiri. JAIMEX-25 (9th edition) took place in October, 2025, near Yokosuka, Japan, featuring the Indian Navy's INS Sahyadri and Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF) units, including the JMSDF Ships Asahi, Oumi and Submarine Jinryu. The exercise focused on advanced anti-submarine warfare, missile defense, and maritime security in the Indo-Pacific.

stem: The I Edition of Joint Table Top Exercise (CINBAX) between the Indian Army and the Cambodian Army was held at :
expl: The 1st edition of Joint Table Top Exercise, CINBAX, between the Indian Army and the Cambodian Army was conducted from 1 to 8 December, 2024 at Foreign Training Node, Pune. Exercise CINBAX was a planning exercise aimed to wargame conduct of Joint Counter Terrorism (CT) operations under Chapter VII of the United Nations Charter. The exercise focussed on discussions pertaining to establishment of Joint Training Task Force for Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance besides planning of operations in CT environment.
